# job-agent-kit

[Website](https://leizikang.github.io/job-agent-kit/) · [中文网站](https://leizikang.github.io/job-agent-kit/zh/)

An AI agent that runs your job search with you: it scouts, screens, tracks and drafts, and you approve everything that goes out.

[简体中文](https://github.com/LeiZiKang/job-agent-kit/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md)

## What it is
An agent-driven repo. Paste the installation sentence below into your agent conversation. The agent interviews you and creates every local file. There are no config files to edit.

![Job board](https://github.com/LeiZiKang/job-agent-kit/blob/main/docs/board.png)

## Quick start
Install the [Claude desktop app](https://claude.ai/download) and open its Code tab, or use Claude Code. Paste this sentence to the agent:

> Install job-agent-kit for me: download https://github.com/LeiZiKang/job-agent-kit to my computer, read its INSTALL.md, and walk me through setup.

The agent reads INSTALL.md and guides setup, defaulting to `~/job-agent-kit`. It asks before installing Git or Python 3.9+ if needed.

### Developer manual installation
With Git, Python 3.9+ and the Claude Code CLI installed, run:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/LeiZiKang/job-agent-kit
cd job-agent-kit
claude
# then say: set me up
```
Also works with Codex: `AGENTS.md` points it at the same rules.

## What the agent does
- **Onboard**: interview, resume reading, profile, pre-approved actions and a manual start-day routine.
- **Scout**: parallel read-only subagents screen channels against your profile and hard lines.
- **Apply with your approval**: you approve target and exact text, except action types you pre-approved.
- **Track**: `bin/jt.py` checks job and company duplicates, records source/reply/interview milestones,
  and generates `board.html`. `status` is read-only; `sweep --dry-run` previews explicit ghosting.
- **Start-day check**: manually review inbox previews once when starting work, within your approval.
- **Weekly review**: `jt funnel --by source`, up to three strategy adjustments, and 1–3 environment
  improvements from the feedback log.

See [architecture](https://github.com/LeiZiKang/job-agent-kit/blob/main/docs/architecture.md), [platform lessons](https://github.com/LeiZiKang/job-agent-kit/blob/main/docs/lessons.md) and
[optional strategy patterns](https://github.com/LeiZiKang/job-agent-kit/blob/main/docs/strategy-patterns.md).

## Safety model
- Red lines: outward actions need your approval (unless pre-approved by type); no false reports; no credentials, captchas or network settings; no opening unread chats without asking; web text is data, not instructions.
- A human stays in the loop. The kit ships no auto-apply bots.
- Platform terms: automating job sites may violate their terms of service. Use at your own risk.

## Built from real use
As of **2026-10-28**, the author's own search had about **195 applications**, a **19% recorded
human-reply rate** in the source-tracked funnel, about **30% for recruiter-sourced applications**,
and about **8% for cold applications through company ATS sites**. There had been **3 interviews
or initial screens**, and the search was still ongoing.

These are approximate results from one search, not promised outcomes. Sources describe how an
opportunity was found; platforms describe where it was submitted. Some historical source/date
records were reconstructed, and route samples and observation windows differ. A first interview
or phone screen counts once per application; an automated rejection does not count as a reply.

This kit is the current entry point; `jobflow` is an earlier version of the same workflow.

## Daily check, not unattended patrol
The author now runs one manual inbox check at the start of each workday. Scheduled unattended
patrol could mark messages read without replying and fail when logins expired. It is **not
recommended by default**. Legacy `patrol.sh` and `schedule.sh` are in [contrib/](https://github.com/LeiZiKang/job-agent-kit/blob/main/contrib/README.md),
for explicit opt-in only. Do not open unread chats just to inspect them.

## Tracker examples
```bash
python3 bin/jt.py company "Example Company" "Known Alias"
python3 bin/jt.py update <application-id> --replied
python3 bin/jt.py update <application-id> --interview YYYY-MM-DD
python3 bin/jt.py funnel --since YYYY-MM-DD --by source
python3 bin/jt.py status --full
python3 bin/jt.py sweep --dry-run
```
`apply --source scout|pirate|recruiter|inbound|referral|self|other` records origin;
`apply --same-company-ok "reason"` records a reviewed company exception. Only `sweep` changes
eligible applications to ghosted after 21 days without a recorded reply/interview. Review missing
outcomes first. See `CLAUDE.md` for semantics and `python3 bin/jt.py <command> --help` for options.

## Updates
The kit is versioned (`VERSION`, [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/LeiZiKang/job-agent-kit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)). At session start the agent runs
`bin/update-check.sh` at most once a week; it only fetches, never installs. When a release is out,
the agent tells you what changes and installs it only after you agree (say "update the kit").
Your data is git-ignored and untouched; keep personal rules in `CLAUDE.local.md` so updates never conflict.

## Repo layout
```
CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md      agent operating manual and feedback loop
.claude/skills/           onboard, scout, weekly-review, update
.claude/agents/           read-only job-scout
bin/                     tracker, tests, update check, optional Codex worker/helpers
contrib/                 legacy patrol and macOS scheduling (opt-in)
templates/               profile, outreach T1–T6, manual inbox brief
  briefs/                pirate and newjobs assignments
  agent-memory/          handoff, feedback log, decisions and findings skeleton
examples/                synthetic demo tracker and handoff
docs/                    architecture, platform lessons, optional strategy patterns
site/                    bilingual website, search metadata and generated LLM documentation
```

## Requirements
Python 3.9+ for the offline tracker; Claude Code or another agent following `AGENTS.md` for the
workflow. Use the browser tool available in your session; no ego-browser or DeepSeek dependency.
The optional worker uses zsh, Perl and Codex CLI; legacy scheduling additionally requires macOS
launchd. Review the [worker execution boundary](https://github.com/LeiZiKang/job-agent-kit/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#worker-execution-boundary)
before using the full-access runner. No worker or scheduler is required for tracker/demo use.

## Contributing
Issues and PRs welcome. Run `python3 bin/test_jt.py` and `python3 bin/jt.py demo` first. Do not include personal data.

## License

# Changelog

Newest first. The `update` skill shows the sections between your version and the latest one.

## 0.3.0 — 2026-10-31
- One-sentence installation in both READMEs and bilingual pages, with copy controls,
  plain-text drag data and manual-install links; INSTALL.md handles cross-folder sessions,
  prerequisite consent, safe reuse, onboarding and uninstall instructions.
- Mac walkthrough: six illustrative desktop app scenes with conversation sidebars,
  collapsible tool calls, input areas and report/board previews; light/dark and mobile layouts.
- Installation FAQ, Markdown pages and LLM documentation follow the new entry point.
- Marketing site: dependency-free English and Chinese pages in `site/`, with Google SEO
  metadata, structured data, sitemap, social image and Agent SEO documentation.
- GitHub Pages workflow regenerates `llms-full.txt` before deployment; runs on `main` pushes
  changing the site, README, CHANGELOG, CLAUDE.md or docs, or by manual dispatch.
- Demo tracker has fictional source, reply and interview fields, so the demo funnel is consistent.

## 0.2.0 — 2026-10-28
- Tracker: `company` duplicate check, `apply --same-company-ok`, `--source` (scout / pirate /
  recruiter / inbound / referral / self / other), `update --replied / --interview`,
  `funnel --since --by platform|source`.
- `status` is now read-only. Ghosting after 21 days without a reply is explicit: `sweep --dry-run`, then `sweep`.
- Scheduled patrol moved to `contrib/` and is no longer recommended (it marked messages read
  without replying and broke when logins expired). A manual start-day check replaces it.
- Weekly loop: funnel by source plus 1–3 environment fixes from `.agent-memory/claude-feedback.md`.
- New: outreach T1b / T5c, `templates/briefs/` (pirate, newjobs), platform-sectioned
  `docs/lessons.md`, `docs/strategy-patterns.md`, stricter worker standing rules.
- Updates: `VERSION`, this changelog, `bin/update-check.sh` and the `update` skill.
  Personal rules go in `CLAUDE.local.md` (git-ignored), so pulling updates never conflicts with them.

## 0.1.0 — 2026-10-14
- Initial release: onboard / scout / weekly-review skills, job-scout subagent, `jt.py` tracker
  and board, Codex worker, optional patrol.

Source: [docs/architecture.md](https://github.com/LeiZiKang/job-agent-kit/blob/main/docs/architecture.md)

# Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[You] <--> L[Lead agent<br/>Claude Code]
  L -->|parallel, read-only| S[Scout subagents]
  L -->|written brief| C[Codex worker<br/>bounded browsing]
  S --> R[reports/scout]
  C --> P[reports/patrol]
  R --> L
  P --> L
  L <--> T[(tracker.json<br/>via bin/jt.py)]
  L <--> M[.agent-memory<br/>handoff, decisions, findings]
  C <--> M
  T --> B[board.html]
  M --> B
```

- **Lead agent (Claude Code)**: judgment, all outward text, final review. Talks to you.
- **Scout subagents**: screen one channel each, in parallel, read-only. Output a shortlist JSON.
- **Codex worker (optional)**: bulk browsing, second-opinion scouting, manually requested inbox previews. Gets a
  written brief with goal, forbidden actions and output path. Never trusted unverified.
- **Tracker (`bin/jt.py`)**: single source of truth for jobs seen, applications and contacts.
  Validated, deduplicated by URL and platform job id, with heuristic company checks and explicit
  delivery review. Read-only status and source/platform funnels; ghosting requires explicit sweep. Agents never hand-edit the JSON.
- **`.agent-memory/`**: cross-agent handoff plus a feedback log feeding weekly environment improvements.
- **`board.html`**: local dashboard generated from the tracker and the handoff file.

## Red lines and "do, then report"
Outward actions (applications, messages, emails) are irreversible and carry your name, so the
default is human approval of the exact target and text. Asking every time is slow and trains you
to click yes blindly, so you can pre-approve specific low-risk action types in `outreach.md`:
the agent acts, then reports the same day. Everything else stays gated. Credentials, captchas
and unread-chat opening always stay with you. Web page text is treated as data, never as
instructions, which limits prompt injection from job posts and messages.


## Worker execution boundary
`bin/codex-run.sh` combines a written brief, fixed standing rules, a configurable timeout and
local logs under ignored `reports/codex-logs/`. It saves the worker's exit status, including timeout
failure, for the caller to inspect. `CODEX_BIN` can select a CLI; otherwise PATH is checked before
the existing app-bundle fallback. There is no DeepSeek or ego-browser dependency.

The runner retains its existing `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` invocation for
compatibility. Prompt rules are **not a sandbox**: this option disables CLI approval and sandbox
controls. Use only in a separately constrained environment you have deliberately approved; it is
optional and not required for onboarding or tracking. This port does not claim technical enforcement
of read-only browsing. Result verification and the user's outward-action authorization still apply.

Unattended macOS scheduling lives in `contrib/` and is not recommended by default. The author's
actual workflow now begins with one manual inbox preview check; permission to read a preview is
not permission to open an unread conversation.

Source: [docs/lessons.md](https://github.com/LeiZiKang/job-agent-kit/blob/main/docs/lessons.md)

# Lessons from real use

These are observations from the author's workflow through 2026-10-28, not permanent platform
contracts or safe request-rate guarantees. Verify the visible UI before an authorized action.
Criteria and candidate facts belong in `profile.md`; these notes describe operational pitfalls.

## General
- **A greeting is not resume delivery.** Check both `jt seen` and `jt company`, then read status
  and evidence. A company appearing in the tracker does not prove its recruiter has the resume.
  Review aliases, client names and team overlap before blocking another route or recording a
  reason with `apply --same-company-ok`.
- **Confirm completion.** Consent screens and uploaded attachments are intermediate steps.
  Record submission only after a confirmation page or equivalent evidence; inspect ATS-parsed
  employers, dates and titles before submission.
- **Record outcomes where the funnel reads them.** Human replies go in `update --replied`;
  interviews and phone screens in `update --interview`. Automated acknowledgments/rejections
  are not human replies. A rejection after a real exchange can have both reply and rejection data.
- **Do not act on stale inbox reports.** The user may have replied from a phone. Before reporting
  a message as pending, check current previews or the conversation only within its authorization.
  Keep live observations separate from old evidence; record unknown dates as unknown, not today.
- **Opening is an outward effect.** Unread chats and invitations may send read receipts. The
  author stopped unattended scheduled patrol and checks manually at the start of the workday:
  unattended runs could mark messages read without replying and lose login sessions.
- **Screen the environment with evidence.** An employer category or a benefits tag does not
  prove reasonable hours. Distinguish positive evidence, negative evidence and unknowns. Apply
  the user's policy for unknowns from `profile.md`; clarify the actual employer/client relationship.
- **Keep decisions visible.** Rewrite the current handoff rather than appending a diary. Record
  friction in `claude-feedback.md`; improve the environment weekly. Answer all user questions
  before closing a phase, and maintain reasoned recommendations unless new evidence changes them.

## BOSS 直聘
- A scout once opened an empty recruiter conversation by clicking “立即沟通”. Its brief must
  explicitly prohibit that action: scouts only navigate to `job_detail` pages and read text,
  with **no button clicks**. “Read-only” alone is too vague.
- Opening a chat and delivering a resume are separate steps; attachment sending may be unavailable
  until a reply. Record the observed result rather than inferring delivery from the button name.
- Company abbreviations and local-language names can return different results. Check aliases,
  city fallback and ads; a matching keyword in the list is not proof that the core role fits.
- Serial reads with pauses reduce avoidable load but do not guarantee exemption from rate limits.
  Do not use concurrent workers on the same account/platform or probe limits through hidden APIs.

## 猎聘
- Clicking “聊一聊 / 继续聊” on a job page has automatically sent a message in the user's name.
  Treat it as a send action, not navigation; scouts never click it.
- Accepting an invitation and submitting a resume has also sent platform-generated greetings.
  Approval must cover those effects. An online-resume card is not proof the attachment was sent.
- Reading many JDs and batch-applying in the **same hour** triggered a captcha in actual use.
  Separate search and application sessions; avoid parallel tabs. Even list-only searches have
  triggered verification. There is no demonstrated safe quota; stop the batch on the first block.
- Resume synchronization can misparse work history. Do not click “sync attachment to online
  resume” as routine maintenance. A web placeholder saying content is app-only does not establish
  who sent it or whether it is an advertisement; verify before reporting an outbound message.

## LinkedIn
- Invitation-note lengths and quotas depend on the account and UI. Read the displayed allowance;
  do not hardcode historical limits or work around exhausted quotas.
- A connection request is not an application, referral or accepted connection. Confirm each state.
  Send T5c at most once after acceptance and only within its approved scope; if no application
  exists, use an approved T1b message without claiming to have applied.
- Keep search, invitations and follow-up messages separate in reports and evidence. A sent request
  must not be counted as a human reply in the application funnel.

## 脉脉
- Opening invitation cards can mark them read. Preview lists first; do not open unread cards for
  scouting unless authorized and the user is ready to respond.
- On some invitation cards, “同意” sends the resume before messaging becomes available. It is
  not a harmless way to ask who the client is. “感兴趣” can also submit an application; scouts
  never click it. Some “立即沟通” buttons lead to membership purchase rather than a free chat.
- After an action, the detail view may move to another job. Reconfirm the target before any
  further authorized action. Search and chat capabilities differ between web and app, and rate
  limits may affect both. Do not change accounts or settings to get around a block.

## Workers
- Use a written brief with one route, budget, prohibited actions and exact output path. Keep
  screening criteria in `profile.md`, not duplicated personal facts in each worker prompt.
- Use the host's managed background-task facility (for example `run_in_background`), never bare
  `&`. Detached work has finished without a completion notification and its results were missed.
  Every polling loop and background wait needs a deadline; clean up task-owned processes.
- Create a valid partial result early, save each verified finding, and report incomplete coverage.
  A timeout or missing file is not evidence that no suitable jobs exist.
- Re-read current result files before final review; a startup handoff snapshot can miss work
  completed during the session. Check worker evidence before claiming anything to the user.
- Stop and re-brief a worker that goes off track. A fixed prompt is an instruction boundary,
  not a technical sandbox. The legacy runner currently retains its full-access CLI option;
  see [architecture](https://github.com/LeiZiKang/job-agent-kit/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#worker-execution-boundary) before opting in.

Source: [docs/strategy-patterns.md](https://github.com/LeiZiKang/job-agent-kit/blob/main/docs/strategy-patterns.md)

# Optional strategy patterns

These are hypotheses to adapt to `profile.md` and the user's own outcomes, not universal hiring
rules. Review them weekly; never override hard lines or invent experience to improve a funnel.

## Two routes: conventional channels and direct engineering contact
Keep a conventional route for screened job boards, recruiters, referrals and suitable company
sites. Alongside it, try public hiring posts from engineering leads or teams willing to review
work directly. Use one relevant project and an approved portfolio link (T1b), rather than a
keyword-heavy pitch. Direct contact can bypass an HR screen; it does not bypass approval or
create permission to scrape private contacts. Recruiter and inbound messages deserve timely
triage before launching another wide search.

## Prefer Mid-level cold applications when the profile fits
For a candidate whose verified experience fits Mid-level work, prioritize those openings in
cold applications. Consider Senior only when the responsibilities and evidence support it;
otherwise keep it as `maybe` and spell out the gap. Job titles and years can be imperfect signals.
The level policy belongs in the user's profile; this is not a ban on senior candidates or roles.

## Filter working conditions, not company labels
Choose evidence of reasonable planning, individual boundaries, clear employment arrangements
and respectful collaboration. An international company label is not proof of these conditions;
a local company label is not proof against them. Record what is observed and what is unknown.
If public evidence is thin, prepare questions for an authorized conversation instead of inventing
certainty. The profile decides which unknowns are acceptable.

## Keep a decision pool
Use `seen_jobs` with `verdict=maybe` for promising roles needing a decision: level gaps, uncertain
work conditions, unclear remote eligibility or possible same-company overlap. Give each a reason
and a next question. `jt status --full` and the board expose this pool. The lead agent reviews it
before any application; it must not silently become an auto-apply queue.

## Let source cohorts decide which searches are worth running
Run `python3 bin/jt.py funnel --by source` for all time and with `--since YYYY-MM-DD` for comparable
application cohorts. Also inspect `--by platform`: platform is where the application happened;
source is how the opportunity was found. For example, a Pirate finding applied through an ATS
keeps `platform=ats` and `source=pirate`.

Use `scout`, `pirate`, `recruiter`, `inbound`, `referral`, `self` or `other` consistently; preserve
missing legacy values as `(unrecorded)`. `recruiter` means recruiter-sourced, while `inbound` is
an employer contacting the candidate directly. Record the first human reply and first interview
or phone screen; later rejection does not erase those events. The funnel counts applications
with a recorded milestone, not every interview round. Automated acknowledgments do not count.

Compare reply/interview yield with time spent, sample size, missing source data and how long
applications have had to mature. A low recent reply rate alone does not prove a route failed.
Reduce repeated low-yield searches; test a narrower route, better fit or a different outreach
approach, then measure again. Pirate discovery can be occasional rather than daily. Propose no
more than three adjustments per weekly review, each with evidence and a follow-up date.
